title: Near or Far?
abstract: Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
journal: Mitigation Measures for Environmental and Humanitarian Disasters

title: Global sensitivity analysis for stochastic models of infectious diseases: Re-emergence of yellow fever virus in the Americas as a case study
abstract: Abstract Emerging infectious diseases are a persistent public health threat that challenge deterministic, mechanistic modeling approaches. Because outbreaks initially start with a low number of infected hosts, their dynamics are highly stochastic, making traditional deterministic methods, e.g. ordinary differential equations, unable to qualitatively or quantitatively capture the transmission dynamics. In place, stochastic models are used, such as Markov chain models, but these models present their own challenges. Often, to infer a quantity of interest with stochastic models, we need to sample the model’s distribution many times over, introducing an additional source of noise to our analysis. This additional noise makes the inference of our quantity of interest more difficult and computationally expensive. Here, we show how novel tools from the field of uncertainty quantification can be used to efficiently separate these two channels of noise, allowing us to make rigorous statistical inferences about processes important for disease emergence. We illustrate these techniques with a model of yellow fever virus spillover in the Americas, a virus that has seen rapid re-emergence amongst multiple hosts and vectors in South America over the last decade. We show that only a handful of parameters’ uncertainties greatly affect variation in cumulative disease incidence. In particular, uncertainty in patch connectivity and non-human primate latency has the greatest impact on the variation of cumulative disease incidence of yellow fever virus across patches. Author Contributions Conceptualization: Nate Kornetzke, Helen J. Methodology: Nate Kornetzke, Helen J. Formal Analysis: Nate Kornetzke. Software: Nate Kornetzke. Visualization: Nate Kornetzke. Writing, Original Draft Preparation: Nate Kornetzke. Writing, Review and Editing: Helen J. Supervision: Helen J. Author Summary Emerging infectious diseases are a growing threat to public health. Computational models allow researchers to forecast future disease burdens and to investigate counterfactual scenarios, and often, these models are stochastic, i.e. contain randomness, to capture the qualitative behavior of emergence. A type of statistical analysis known as global sensitivity analysis allows modelers to rigorously analyze how varying the input to a model affects variation in its outputs. This type of analysis helps us infer what mechanisms are important for disease mitigation and control, especially when an infectious disease has a complex ecology consisting of multiple hosts and vectors. Until recently, stochastic models of emerging infectious diseases often proved too computationally expensive to perform a global sensitivity analysis on. Here, we demonstrate how new mathematical tools allow us to streamline this process for complex models of emerging infectious diseases. We analyze the ecology of re-emerging yellow fever in South America, a public health threat occurring in many hosts and vectors across vastly different ecosystems.

title: EFEKTIVITAS DAUN MENGKUDU (Morinda citrifolia L.) SEBAGAI INSEKTISIDA NABATI TERHADAP MORTALITAS LARVA NYAMUK Aedes aegypti
abstract: Dengue remains a public health concern, highlighting the need to develop alternative approaches for controlling Aedes aegypti larvae and reducing reliance on synthetic larvicides. This study aimed to evaluate the larvicidal activity of noni leaf extract (Morinda citrifolia L.) against third- and fourth-instar Aedes aegypti larvae and identify the most efficient concentration among those tested. A laboratory experimental design was employed with six treatment groups: noni leaf extract at concentrations of 30%, 35%, 40%, and 45%, a negative control consisting of 0.9% NaCl solution, and a positive control consisting of abate. Each group contained 25 larvae and was tested in four replicates. Larval mortality was observed after 24 and 48 hours and analyzed descriptively. The results showed that all extract concentrations produced 100% larval mortality within 24 hours, equivalent to the positive control. In contrast, no larval mortality occurred in the negative control. The same mortality pattern was observed after 48 hours. These findings indicate that noni leaf extract exhibited larvicidal activity at all tested concentrations. The 30% concentration was the most efficient within the tested range because it achieved maximum mortality. Further testing at lower concentrations and under field conditions is necessary to determine the minimum effective concentration and assess its practical applicability. ABSTRAK Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) masih menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat sehingga pengendalian larva Aedes aegypti perlu dikembangkan melalui alternatif yang berpotensi mengurangi ketergantungan pada larvasida sintetis. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis efektivitas ekstrak daun mengkudu (Morinda citrifolia L.) terhadap mortalitas larva Aedes aegypti instar III–IV serta mengidentifikasi konsentrasi paling efisien di antara konsentrasi yang diuji. Penelitian menggunakan rancangan eksperimen laboratorium dengan enam kelompok perlakuan, yaitu ekstrak daun mengkudu konsentrasi 30%, 35%, 40%, dan 45%, kontrol negatif berupa larutan NaCl 0,9%, serta kontrol positif berupa abate. Setiap kelompok diuji menggunakan 25 larva dengan empat kali pengulangan. Pengamatan mortalitas dilakukan setelah 24 dan 48 jam, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh konsentrasi ekstrak menghasilkan mortalitas larva sebesar 100% setelah 24 jam, sama dengan kontrol positif. Sebaliknya, kontrol negatif tidak menunjukkan kematian larva. Pola mortalitas yang sama ditemukan pada pengamatan 48 jam. Dengan demikian, ekstrak daun mengkudu menunjukkan aktivitas larvasida pada seluruh konsentrasi yang diuji. Konsentrasi 30% merupakan konsentrasi paling efisien dalam rentang pengujian karena telah menghasilkan mortalitas maksimum. Pengujian konsentrasi lebih rendah dan evaluasi lapangan diperlukan untuk menentukan konsentrasi efektif minimum serta potensi penerapannya.

source_records.abstract: Dengue remains a public health concern, highlighting the need to develop alternative approaches for controlling Aedes aegypti larvae and reducing reliance on synthetic larvicides. This study aimed to evaluate the larvicidal activity of noni leaf extract (Morinda citrifolia L.) against third- and fourth-instar Aedes aegypti larvae and identify the most efficient concentration among those tested. A laboratory experimental design was employed with six treatment groups: noni leaf extract at concentrations of 30%, 35%, 40%, and 45%, a negative control consisting of 0.9% NaCl solution, and a positive control consisting of abate. Each group contained 25 larvae and was tested in four replicates. Larval mortality was observed after 24 and 48 hours and analyzed descriptively. The results showed that all extract concentrations produced 100% larval mortality within 24 hours, equivalent to the positive control. In contrast, no larval mortality occurred in the negative control. The same mortality pattern was observed after 48 hours. These findings indicate that noni leaf extract exhibited larvicidal activity at all tested concentrations. The 30% concentration was the most efficient within the tested range because it achieved maximum mortality. Further testing at lower concentrations and under field conditions is necessary to determine the minimum effective concentration and assess its practical applicability. title: Two chromosome-scale genomes of wild Aedes aegypti aegypti mosquitoes from North America and South-East Asia.
abstract: The yellow fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti) is the primary vector for diseases such as chikungunya, dengue fever, yellow fever, and Zika fever. These mosquitoes have been designated as two subspecies: Ae. aegypti formosus (Aaf) and Ae. aegypti aegypti (Aaa)-the former being a darker form limited to sub-Saharan Africa and the latter referring to lighter colored individuals found circumglobally in the tropics and sub-tropics. In addition to morphology and distribution, these two sub-species differ in their behavior and ecology-Aaf females generally feed on nonhuman mammals and live in rural and sylvatic areas, whereas Aaa females preferentially feed on humans and are found in human dwellings in urban areas. These characteristics and differences make them species of great medical importance, and the development of resources for understanding their biology has high priority. We recently published a chromosome-scale wild Aaf genome assembly and here we add to this body of resources by presenting two de novo chromosome-scale genome assemblies of wild-caught Aaa from North America and Southeast Asia. Using the Pacific Biosciences HiFi sequencing platform combined with HiC sequencing, we achieved high continuity (N50: >400 Mb; L50: 2) and completeness (BUSCO single-copy: ~97%; diptera set). These assemblies will contribute to further elucidate the global genetic diversity of this major disease vector and uncover the genetic basis of phenotypic differences between the sub-species.

title: Pemberdayaan Masyarakat dengan Gerakan Pemberantasan Sarang Nyamuk (PSN) dan Survey Vektor DBD
abstract: This community service activity aimed to improve students’ knowledge and awareness of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) prevention through the Mosquito Nest Eradication Movement (PSN), vector surveys, epidemiological investigations, and early detection of DHF. The activity was conducted on August 29–30, 2026, at SMA Negeri 4 Manado, involving 60 students in collaboration with healthcare workers, Ranomut Community Health Center, the Manado City Health Office, and school representatives. The implementation methods included preparation, health education, vector surveys, follow-up actions, and evaluation. The educational materials covered the 3M Plus approach, identification of mosquito breeding sites, dengue transmission prevention, epidemiological investigations, and recognition of DHF symptoms and warning signs. The results showed that PSN education and vector surveys were conducted according to the planned topics. The survey found no mosquito larvae in potential breeding sites within the school environment, which was attributed to the dry season. This activity is expected to encourage students and school personnel to actively maintain environmental cleanliness and implement PSN measures sustainably.

title: Analisis Spatial Autoregressive (Sar) Pada Kasus Tbc di Provinsi Jawa Barat
abstract: ABSTRACT Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant public health problem in West Java Province, with the distribution of the TB Case Detection Rate varying across districts and cities. As an infectious disease, TB transmission is closely related to geographic proximity and interactions among populations, meaning that TB incidence in one area may be influenced by conditions in neighboring areas, indicating the presence of spatial dependence that needs to be considered in statistical analysis. This study aims to analyze the spatial pattern of the TB Case Detection Rate and identify health and housing condition factors that influence TB across 27 districts/cities in West Java Province in 2024. The study uses secondary data on the TB Case Detection Rate and related explanatory variables. Spatial autocorrelation was tested using Moran’s Index, while an inverse distance spatial weight matrix was applied to represent geographic proximity and the potential for interregional transmission. Prior to spatial modeling, classical assumptions were tested and satisfied. Model selection was conducted using the Lagrange Multiplier (LM) test and the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), which indicated that the Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) model was the most appropriate. The results show a significant spatial autocorrelation in the TB Case Detection Rate, confirming the need for spatial regression analysis. The SAR model estimation indicates that the TB Case Detection Rate is significantly influenced by neighboring regions. Additionally, the number of new HIV/AIDS cases has a positive effect on TB, while malaria morbidity rate, dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) incidence rate, and the percentage of households living in adequate housing have negative effects on the TB Case Detection Rate. Diagnostic tests indicate that the residuals of the SAR model are normally distributed and homoscedastic. These findings highlight the importance of a spatial approach in TB analysis due to the potential spread of the disease across geographically adjacent areas. The negative relationship between TB and malaria as well as dengue reflects differences in regional characteristics, where areas with high TB rates tend to have environmental and epidemiological conditions different from those in malaria- and dengue-endemic regions. Therefore, TB control policies should consider spatial linkages and regional characteristics. Keywords: Tuberculosis, Spatial Autoregressive, Moran’s Index, Inverse Distance. ABSTRAK Tuberkulosis (TBC) masih menjadi permasalahan kesehatan masyarakat yang signifikan di Provinsi Jawa Barat, dengan distribusi Angka Penemuan TBC yang tidak merata antar kabupaten/kota. Mengingat TBC merupakan penyakit menular yang penyebarannya berkaitan erat dengan kedekatan geografis dan interaksi antarpenduduk, maka kejadian TBC di suatu wilayah berpotensi dipengaruhi oleh wilayah di sekitarnya sehingga menunjukkan adanya ketergantungan spasial yang perlu diperhitungkan dalam analisis statistik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pola spasial Angka Penemuan TBC serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor kesehatan dan kondisi perumahan yang memengaruhi TBC di 27 kabupaten/kota di Provinsi Jawa Barat tahun 2024. Penelitian menggunakan data sekunder Angka Penemuan TBC dan variabel penjelas terkait, dengan pengujian autokorelasi spasial menggunakan Indeks Moran serta matriks bobot spasial inverse distance untuk merepresentasikan kedekatan geografis dan potensi penyebaran antarwilayah. Sebelum pemodelan spasial dilakukan, asumsi klasik diuji dan terpenuhi, sementara pemilihan model dilakukan menggunakan uji Lagrange Multiplier (LM) dan nilai Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) yang menunjukkan bahwa model Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) merupakan model terbaik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan adanya autokorelasi spasial yang signifikan pada Angka Penemuan TBC sehingga analisis regresi spasial diperlukan, dengan hasil estimasi model SAR yang menunjukkan bahwa Angka Penemuan TBC dipengaruhi secara signifikan oleh wilayah sekitarnya. Selain itu, jumlah kasus baru HIV/AIDS berpengaruh positif terhadap TBC, sedangkan angka kesakitan malaria dan demam berdarah dengue (DBD) serta persentase rumah tangga yang menempati rumah layak huni berpengaruh negatif terhadap Angka Penemuan TBC. Uji diagnostik menunjukkan bahwa residual model SAR berdistribusi normal dan bersifat homogen. Hasil penelitian ini menegaskan pentingnya pendekatan spasial dalam analisis TBC karena sifat penularannya memungkinkan penyebaran antarwilayah yang berdekatan, sementara hubungan negatif antara TBC dengan malaria dan DBD mencerminkan perbedaan karakteristik wilayah, di mana daerah dengan TBC tinggi cenderung memiliki kondisi lingkungan dan epidemiologi yang berbeda dengan wilayah endemis malaria dan DBD, sehingga kebijakan pengendalian TBC perlu mempertimbangkan keterkaitan spasial serta karakteristik regional. Kata Kunci: Tuberkulosis, Spatial Autoregressive, Indeks Moran, Inverse Distance.

title: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Secondary to Tropical Infections: A Case Series from a Tertiary Care Hospital
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) can be triggered by various infections, including tropical illnesses like dengue fever and scrub typhus.This series included five children with secondary HLH associated with tropical illnessess.The cohort included three girls and two boys aged 1-13 years.Two cases were associated with dengue fever and three with scrub typhus.All children met at least five of the HLH-2004 diagnostic criteria.The study underscores the importance of considering HLH in children with prolonged febrile illness in endemic regions and highlights the clinical improvement of pulse steroid therapy in such cases.
journal: Imsang soa hyeoraek jong-yang/Imsang soa hyeol'aeg jong'yang/Clinical pediatric hematology-oncology

title: Chip-Integrated Optical Modulation Biosensing with Microfluidic Background Reduction for High-Sensitivity Fluorescence Immunoassays
abstract: Microfluidic fluorescence immunoassays enable sensitive biomarker detection, but performance is limited by inefficient capture on planar surfaces and background fluorescence from unbound labels. Here, we present chip-based optical modulation biosensing (Chip-OMB), combining three-dimensional magnetic bead-based target capture, bead immobilization, internal fluid flushing, and modulated optical background subtraction. Magnetic beads are concentrated and immobilized in the chamber, while controlled on-chip flushing displaces unbound fluorescent labels without requiring user-performed washing after chip loading. Alternating optical interrogation of the bead cluster and surrounding solution enables background subtraction. Using fluorescently labeled magnetic beads, Chip-OMB achieved limits of detection of 0.1 pM in buffer and 22 pM in undiluted plasma, corresponding to 580-fold and 22-fold lower equivalent fluorophore-concentration limits of detection, respectively, than conventional steady-state bulk fluorescence measurements using a plate reader. Measurements correlated with the laboratory optical modulation biosensing system (R2 = 0.98). In an anti-dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) immunoglobulin G (IgG) immunoassay, Chip-OMB achieved a 3 ng/mL limit of detection with a ~4-log dynamic range. Among 56 sera, 29 DENV-2 cases confirmed by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were Panbio IgG-positive and above the exploratory Chip-OMB cutoff, while all 27 study-defined negative controls were below it.

title: Diagnóstico e intervención de enfermedades infecciosas desatendidas y crónicas no trasmisibles prevalentes en poblaciones en riesgo de la parroquia Sucre del Cantón 24 de Mayo.
abstract: Neglected infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases constitute two major public health challenges; Diabetes Mellitus follows a prolonged, progressive course, whereas dengue is vector-borne, increasing the epidemiological burden and complicating laboratory diagnosis. The study aimed to analyze the laboratory diagnosis and intervention regarding prevalent neglected infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases in at-risk populations within the Sucre parish of the 24 de Mayo Canton. An observational, analytical, cross-sectional, and prospective methodology was implemented using a convenience sample of 37 participants selected according to inclusion and exclusion criteria; ethics committee approval was obtained, ensuring compliance with all established requirements. Results demonstrated a dengue prevalence of 5.4% (n=2) with 97.3% (n=36) serological evidence of IgG antibodies and a Diabetes Mellitus prevalence of 5.4% (n=2), with a female predominance in both conditions. Statistical analysis revealed no significant association between dengue and Diabetes Mellitus (p=0.848/ns). An educational intervention trained 100% of the participants, strengthening disease prevention and self-care practices. The study concluded that the at-risk population exhibits a low prevalence of active dengue alongside previous viral exposure and an emerging risk of prediabetes both more pronounced in women with no direct statistical association between the two diseases; these laboratory findings support the null hypothesis, underscoring the need for sustained preventive strategies.

title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti
abstract: The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the primary vector for arboviruses that are pathogenic to humans, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses. Following a blood meal, arboviruses initially infect the midgut, disseminate systemically to the carcass, and eventually reach the salivary glands for transmission. Here, we investigate tissue-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA) activity and test whether enhancing this pathway can restrict arbovirus infection. Our results show that salivary glands are less refractory to arboviral infection relative to the carcass, with low expression patterns of siRNA pathway genes. Transgenic overexpression of Dicer-2 , a key component of the siRNA pathway, in salivary glands leads to a significant decrease in orthoflavivirus and alphavirus replication. DENV4 small RNA sequencing reveals altered viral RNA processing and increased levels of 21-nt virus-derived siRNAs. Conversely, Dicer-2 overexpression in the fat body, a major carcass tissue, only moderately suppresses dengue and Mayaro virus infection. Notably, simultaneous overexpression of Dicer-2 in both midguts and salivary glands produces the strongest reduction in viral load in saliva, indicating reduced transmission potential. These findings reveal tissue-specific differences in antiviral pathway activity and demonstrate that targeted enhancement of salivary gland antiviral defense can restrict arbovirus transmission.

source_records.title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti
source_records.abstract: Abstract Arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), pose a significant global health and economic burden, with Aedes aegypti serving as their primary vector. Arbovirus infection in Ae. aegypti progresses sequentially through the midgut (MG), carcass (CA), and salivary glands (SG), with each tissue exhibiting distinct antiviral responses. Here, we investigate tissue-specific antiviral mechanisms, focusing on the small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathway in SGs. Our results reveal that SGs possess weaker antiviral defense and are more susceptible to arboviral infection compared to MGs and CAs. Notably, overexpression of Dicer2 ( Dcr2 ), a key component of the siRNA pathway, in SGs leads to a significant decrease in arboviral replication. Conversely, Dcr2 overexpression in fat bodies, the primary tissue in CAs, only moderately suppresses DENV2 infection and has no notable effect on Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection. Remarkably, the simultaneous overexpression of Dcr2 in both MGs and SGs enhances antiviral activity, effectively blocking the transmission of multiple arboviruses. These findings reveal the tissue-specific dynamics of mosquito antiviral immunity and underscore the potential for targeting SG-specific immunity to disrupt arbovirus transmission, providing a promising approach for controlling mosquito-borne diseases.

title: Diagnóstico inmunoserológico de enfermedades infecciosas prevalentes en habitantes de las Ciudadelas 3 de mayo y 10 agosto, Cantón Jipijapa.
abstract: Infectious diseases continue to pose a public health challenge due to their transmission and the influence of social, environmental, and biological factors. This study aimed to determine, using immunoserological or molecular methods, the prevalence of infectious diseases among residents of the Ciudadelas 3 de mayo and 10 de agosto neighborhoods in the Jipijapa canton. A descriptive, observational, and cross-sectional study was conducted, with a reference population of 46,429 inhabitants according to the 2022 Census. A stratified probability sampling method was used to establish a general sample of 650 people, from which 52 residents of the Dr. Miguel Morán Lucio urban parish were selected for this study, of whom 40 were women and 12 were men. The results showed a higher representation of individuals with secondary education (67.3%) and those in the 46-60 age group (51.9%). The identified prevalence was 1.9% for dengue and 11.5% for Helicobacter pylori, while rotavirus, adenovirus, and Salmonella showed no positive cases. It is concluded that the prevalence of the diseases evaluated was low; therefore, it is recommended to strengthen community surveillance and maintain ongoing prevention and health education efforts.

title: A broadly active flavivirus NS4B targeting compound that blocks NS4B-NS3 binding and replication organelle formation
abstract: Abstract Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses, including West Nile virus (WNV), dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), cause substantial global morbidity and mortality, yet no broadly effective direct-acting antivirals are available. The viral nonstructural protein NS4B has emerged as a promising antiviral target, although the compounds described to date are largely DENV-specific. Here we characterize SRI-38841, a xanthine analog derived from hit-to-lead optimization of a previously described WNV inhibitor, which inhibits WNV replication with an IC90 of 0.87 μM and low cytotoxicity, and retains activity against DENV, ZIKV, and JEV. Serial passage of WNV under compound selection yielded resistant viruses bearing mutations in NS4B, and reverse genetics was used to confirm the role of individual amino acid substitutions. Several of these residues map to regions analogous to those implicated in resistance to the DENV NS4B inhibitors JNJ-A07 and NITD-688. Docking of SRI-38841 to an AlphaFold2 model of WNV NS4B predicted a binding pocket within a cytosolic-facing funnel, and mutation of the pocket residues A45 and K56 likewise conferred resistance, while changes at Q170 and T220 did not. Together, these data favor a topology model in which the compound engages a cytosolic-facing pocket over one placing these residues in the ER lumen. Mechanistically, SRI-38841 disrupts the NS4B–NS3 interaction and abolishes replication organelle formation in infected cells. Unlike JNJ-A07 and NITD-688, which were inactive against WNV and ZIKV, SRI-38841 inhibits all four viruses tested, identifying this xanthine class as a starting point for broadly active orthoflavivirus antivirals. Importance Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses such as West Nile virus (WNV), dengue virus (DENV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) remain a substantial global health burden, and no broadly effective direct-acting antivirals are available. NS4B has emerged as one of the most promising targets in this space, but the inhibitors described to date, including the clinical-stage compounds JNJ-A07/JNJ-1802 and NITD-688, are largely DENV-specific. An antiviral with genuine pan-orthoflavivirus activity has been lacking. In this study we characterize SRI-38841, a xanthine analog arising from hit-to-lead optimization of a WNV inhibitor we previously described. SRI-38841 has broad spectrum activity, showing efficacy against DENV2, ZIKV, and JEV as well as WNV. It targets the NS4B protein, and and the resistance landscape converges with that of the aforementioned DENV inhibitors. Finally, docking of SRI-38841 against an AlphaFold2 model predicted a binding pocket within a cytosolic-facing funnel. These results favor the NMR/computational topology model over one placing these residues in the ER lumen — a distinction with direct consequences for how this inhibitor class is understood and optimized.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革病毒 1-4 和登革热疾病仍然是全球重大健康负担,并且没有广泛有效的直接作用 抗病毒药物。病毒非结构蛋白 NS4B 已成为该领域最有前途的靶点之一,但迄今为止描述的抑制剂,包括临床阶段化合物 JNJ-A07/JNJ-1802 和 NITD-688,很大程度上是 DENV 特异性的。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究描述了 SRI-38841 的特征,它是一种黄嘌呤类似物,源自先前描述的 WNV 抑制剂的命中至先导优化,它能抑制 WNV 复制,IC90 为 0.87 μM,细胞毒性低,并保留针对 DENV、ZIKV 和 JEV 的活性。WNV 在化合物选择下的连续传代产生了 NS4B 中带有 突变 的抗性病毒,并使用反向遗传学来确认单个氨基酸取代的作用。
elements_zh.methods: SRI-38841 通过先前描述的 WNV 抑制剂的命中到先导优化来表征。在化合物选择下连续传代西尼罗河病毒用于鉴定抗性病毒,并采用反向遗传学来确认单个氨基酸取代在抗性中的作用。SRI-38841 与 WNV NS4B 的 AlphaFold2 模型的对接预测了面向胞质的漏斗内的结合袋。
elements_zh.main_results: 其中一些残基映射到与 DENV NS4B 抑制剂 JNJ-A07 和 NITD-688 抗性相关的区域类似的区域。口袋残基 A45 和 K56 的 突变 同样赋予抗性,而 Q170 和 T220 的变化则没有。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果有利于 NMR/计算拓扑模型,而不是将这些残基置于 ER 腔中——这一区别直接影响了如何理解和优化此类抑制剂。与对 WNV 和 ZIKV 无活性的 JNJ-A07 和 NITD-688 不同,SRI-38841 可抑制所有四种测试的病毒,从而将黄嘌呤类确定为具有广泛活性的正黄病毒 抗病毒药物 的起点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,SRI-38841 是开发广泛活性的正黄病毒 抗病毒药物 的有希望的候选者,这可能对 登革病毒 感染的 治疗 和其他相关黄病毒产生重大影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,结果来自体外实验。由于缺乏详细的临床或体内数据,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究描述了 SRI-38841 的特征,它是一种黄嘌呤类似物,源自先前描述的 WNV 抑制剂的命中至先导优化,它能抑制 WNV 复制,IC90 为 0.87 μM,细胞毒性低,并保留针对 DENV、ZIKV 和 JEV 的活性。WNV 在化合物选择下的连续传代产生了 NS4B 中带有 突变 的抗性病毒,并使用反向遗传学来确认单个氨基酸取代的作用。
analysis_zh.methods: SRI-38841 通过先前描述的 WNV 抑制剂的命中到先导优化来表征。在化合物选择下连续传代西尼罗河病毒用于鉴定抗性病毒,并采用反向遗传学来确认单个氨基酸取代在抗性中的作用。SRI-38841 与 WNV NS4B 的 AlphaFold2 模型的对接预测了面向胞质的漏斗内的结合袋。
analysis_zh.main_results: 其中一些残基映射到与 DENV NS4B 抑制剂 JNJ-A07 和 NITD-688 抗性相关的区域类似的区域。口袋残基 A45 和 K56 的 突变 同样赋予抗性,而 Q170 和 T220 的变化则没有。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果有利于 NMR/计算拓扑模型,而不是将这些残基置于 ER 腔中——这一区别直接影响了如何理解和优化此类抑制剂。与对 WNV 和 ZIKV 无活性的 JNJ-A07 和 NITD-688 不同,SRI-38841 可抑制所有四种测试的病毒,从而将黄嘌呤类确定为具有广泛活性的正黄病毒 抗病毒药物 的起点。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,SRI-38841 是开发广泛活性的正黄病毒 抗病毒药物 的有希望的候选者,这可能对 登革病毒 感染的 治疗 和其他相关黄病毒产生重大影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,结果来自体外实验。由于缺乏详细的临床或体内数据,证据强度中等。

title: Diagnóstico e intervención de enfermedades infecciosas desatendidas y crónicas no transmisibles prevalentes en poblaciones vulnerables de la Parroquia San Lorenzo de Jipijapa.
abstract: Neglected infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases, such as dengue and diabetes mellitus constitute significant public health concerns due to their clinical, social, and epidemiological impact, particularly in tropical settings and socioeconomic disadvantaged contexts, where the coexistence of both conditions represents an important risk because of the metabolic and immunological alterations that may arise. The aim of this study was to analyze the diagnosis and intervention of prevalent neglected infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases among vulnerable populations in the San Lorenzo parish of Jipijapa. The methodology employed was observational, analytical, cross-sectional, and prospective in nature, using a convenience sample of 40 vulnerable participants residing in Jipijapa, including 21 women (52.5%) and 19 men (47.5%), selected according to inclusion and exclusion criteria. The project complied with the requirements established by the ethics committee. The results showed an active dengue prevalence of 5% (n = 2) and a high rate of previous exposure of 87.5%, while diabetes mellitus also presented a prevalence of 5% (n = 2), with glucose levels >126 mg/dL. No statistically significant association was found between the two conditions (p = 0.739). It was possible to intervene in 100% of the planned population through community training sessions, with balanced participation between men and women, thereby strengthening health promotion within the community. In conclusion, although the frequency was low, both diseases remain present in the vulnerable population; therefore, it is recommended to strengthen vector control, glucose screening, and educational programs aimed at prevention, early detection, and community self-care.

The results showed an active dengue prevalence of 5% (n = 2) and a high rate of previous exposure of 87.5%, while diabetes mellitus also presented a prevalence of 5% (n = 2), with glucose levels >126 mg/dL. No statistically significant association was found between the two conditions (p = 0.739). It was possible to intervene in 100% of the planned population through community training sessions, with balanced participation between men and women, thereby strengthening health promotion within the community. In conclusion, although the frequency was low, both diseases remain present in the vulnerable population; therefore, it is recommended to strengthen vector control, glucose screening, and educational programs aimed at prevention, early detection, and community self-care.

title: Diagnostico e intervención de enfermedades infecciosas desatendidas y crónicas no transmisibles prevalentes en población en riesgo de la Ciudadela Cristo del Consuelo Canton Jipijapa.
abstract: Las enfermedades infecciosas desatendidas y las enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles representan un importante problema de salud pública en poblaciones vulnerables. El objetivo del estudio fue analizar el diagnóstico e intervención del dengue y la diabetes mellitus en la población en riesgo de la ciudadela Cristo del Consuelo, cantón Jipijapa. Se realizó una investigación observacional, analítica, transversal y prospectiva en 37 participantes seleccionados mediante criterios de inclusión y exclusión. Para el diagnóstico se emplearon pruebas inmunológicas para dengue (NS1) y determinación de glucosa sérica para diabetes mellitus; además, se desarrolló una intervención educativa mediante conferencias dirigidas a la comunidad. Se encontró una prevalencia de dengue del 2,7 % y de diabetes mellitus del 16,22 %, identificándose una asociación estadísticamente significativa entre ambas enfermedades (p=0,021). La intervención alcanzó una cobertura del 100 % de la población participante, fortaleciendo los conocimientos sobre prevención y control. Se concluye que la coexistencia de dengue y diabetes mellitus constituye un problema de salud pública en la población estudiada, por lo que es necesario fortalecer las estrategias de diagnóstico oportuno, vigilancia epidemiológica, prevención y educación sanitaria, con el propósito de disminuir las complicaciones, mejorar la calidad de vida y promover comunidades más saludables y resilientes en la comunidad estudiada.

title: Molecular Surveillance for Oropouche, Mayaro, West Nile, and Saint Louis EncephalitisViruses, Brazil, 2019–2025
abstract: To assess the circulation of Oropouche, Mayaro, West Nile, and St. Louis encephalitis viruses, we tested samples from 824 patients with acute febrile illness, 3,484 mosquitoes, and 113 nonhuman primates from northern Minas Gerais, Brazil. All samples were negative for dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika virus. One imported Oropouche virus infection was detected.

title: Diagnóstico inmunoserológico o molecular de enfermedades infecciosas prevalentes en habitantes de las parroquias La América, Julcuy, La Unión y Membrillal.
abstract: Infectious diseases represent a persistent challenge for rural communities, where living conditions and limited access to basic services threaten their health. The objective was to determine the immunoserological or molecular diagnosis of prevalent infectious diseases in inhabitants of the parishes of La América, Julcuy, La Unión, and Membrillal. Methodologically, a quantitative, descriptive, observational, cross-sectional approach was used, with a stratified sampling of 60 participants.The results showed that sociodemographic and socioeconomic factors reflect a predominantly adult and single population, with incomes of less than $100 (68.3%) and critical deficiencies in sanitation (26.7%) and access to drinking water (20.0%). In viral agents, the prevalence was zero (0.0%) for dengue NS1, rotavirus, and adenovirus.in bacterial agents, the total prevalence of Helicobacter pylori was 25% (n=15). Regarding the detection of Salmonella spp., there was a low incidence of 1.66% (n=1). It is concluded that the presence of these agents is linked to local risk factors, underscoring the need to strengthen laboratory monitoring to prevent infectious outbreaks in these parishes, despite the low prevalence of active cases detected at the time of sampling.

title: Climate change and extreme weather events to intensify West Nile virus activity
abstract: Abstract Vector-borne zoonotic diseases pose a substantive risk to public health worldwide, yet predicting outbreaks at scales useful for public health response remains a critical challenge. Transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, West Nile virus is the leading cause of arboviral disease in the United States, progressing to neuroinvasive disease in approximately 1% of infections. Arizona’s record-breaking 2021 outbreak, with 1,715 reported human cases and 127 deaths exemplifies this growing burden. Using a decade of mosquito surveillance data coupled with time-lagged weather patterns in a random forest framework, we developed spatial models predicting Culex abundance and West Nile virus occurrence across Arizona at weekly temporal and fine spatial resolution. Our weighted models classified viral occurrence with 98.9% accuracy and explained 65.3% of weekly variation in county-level human cases, with human cases lagging modeled activity by one week. Neither mosquito abundance nor viral occurrence declined at the extreme temperatures characteristic of Arizona summers, suggesting that thermal refugia sustain transmission. Drought-monsoon cycling, rather than temperature alone, emerged as the primary driver of West Nile activity, and projections through 2100 indicate intensifying activity under all climate change scenarios.

title: Household Container Characteristics Associated with Mosquito Larval Presence in a Highland Community of Tana Toraja, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: Dengue continues to pose a major mosquito-borne public health problem in tropical countries, including Indonesia, where household water containers frequently serve as habitats for mosquito larvae. However, studies examining household container characteristics associated with mosquito larval presence in highland communities remain limited. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Bombongan Urban Village, Makale District, Tana Toraja Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The study included 100 households and 128 water-holding containers. Container type, functional container category, container condition, and mosquito larval presence were recorded through direct field observation. Associations were examined using Pearson’s chi-square test and a binary logistic generalized estimating equations (GEE) model to account for household-level clustering. Results: Of the 128 inspected water-holding containers, 89 (69.5%) were positive for mosquito larvae, and 94 (73.4%) were open. At the household level, 71 of 100 households had at least one larva-positive container, resulting in a House Index of 71.0%, a Container Index of 69.5%, and a Breteau Index of 89. Discarded containers had the highest proportion of larval positivity (91.7%), whereas animal drinking containers were the most frequently observed type. Functional container category was associated with larval presence in the bivariate analysis (p = 0.025) and remained significant as an overall variable in the GEE model (Wald χ2 = 12.178, df = 3, p = 0.007), although none of the individual categories differed significantly from animal drinking containers. title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Analisis ANALISIS HUBUNGAN KEJADIAN BANJIR DAN PENYAKIT BERBASIS LINGKUNGAN MENGGUNAKAN SIG DI KECAMATAN NGALIYAN KOTA SEMARANG
abstract: dengan kejadian banjir yang relatif tinggi, sedangkan banjir berpotensi meningkatkan risiko penyakit berbasis lingkungan seperti diare, leptospirosis, dan demam berdarah dengue (DBD).Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara tingkat kejadian banjir dan Incidence Rate (IR) penyakit berbasis lingkungan pada 10 kelurahan di Kecamatan Ngaliyan tahun 2025.Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kuantitatif dengan analisis spasial berbasis Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG), berupa pemetaan dan overlay, serta uji korelasi Spearman Rank.Data kejadian banjir diperoleh dari BPBD Kota Semarang dan data kasus penyakit dari puskesmas di wilayah Kecamatan Ngaliyan; seluruh kelurahan dianalisis dengan teknik sampling jenuh.Sepanjang tahun 2025 tercatat 2.041 kasus diare, 5 kasus leptospirosis, dan 10 kasus DBD.Tujuh kelurahan berkategori banjir tinggi, satu sedang, dan dua rendah.Analisis overlay menunjukkan kesesuaian pola banjir dan penyakit hanya pada sebagian kelurahan.Uji Spearman Rank menghasilkan r = 0,422 (p = 0,224) untuk IR diare, r = -0,574 (p = 0,083) untuk IR leptospirosis, dan r = -0,307 (p = 0,338) untuk IR DBD, sehingga tidak terdapat hubungan yang signifikan secara statistik (p > 0,05).Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa banjir bukan satu-satunya penentu sebaran penyakit berbasis lingkungan; faktor sanitasi, kualitas air, vektor, dan perilaku masyarakat perlu dipertimbangkan dalam penelitian dan pengendalian selanjutnya.

title: Implementasi Siyaga (Surveilans Nyamuk Berbasis Rumah Tangga) Menggunakan Ovitrap Di Kota Bengkulu
abstract: Demam berdarah dengue masih menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat yang dipengaruhi oleh tingginya kepadatan vektor dan rendahnya keterlibatan masyarakat dalam pengendalian lingkungan. Di wilayah kerja Puskesmas Kampung Bali, Kota Bengkulu, capaian Angka Bebas Jentik (ABJ) masih berfluktuasi antara 70%–87%, berada di bawah target nasional (≥95%), sehingga diperlukan penguatan surveilans dan pemberdayaan masyarakat dalam pengendalian vektor. Program SIYAGA (Surveilans Nyamuk Berbasis Rumah Tangga) bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan, keterampilan, dan partisipasi masyarakat dalam surveilans serta pengendalian vektor DBD berbasis ovitrap. Kegiatan dilaksanakan melalui edukasi kesehatan, pelatihan pembuatan ovitrap, pemasangan pada 40 rumah tangga, serta pemantauan selama empat minggu. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui perbandingan hasil sebelum dan sesudah, observasi keterampilan pemasangan Ovitrap, serta pemantauan Ovitrap Index (OI). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa skor pengetahuan peserta (n=40) meningkat dari rata-rata 50,3 ± 12,4 pada pre-test menjadi 88,1 ± 8,6 pada post-test. Sebagian besar peserta mampu memasang ovitrap dengan benar dan 90,0% peserta mengikuti seluruh tahapan kegiatan yang meliputi edukasi, pelatihan pembuatan ovitrap, pemasangan ovitrap, dan minimal tiga dari empat kali pemantauan mingguan. Nilai Ovitrap Index meningkat dari 52,5% pada minggu pertama menjadi 62,5% pada minggu keempat, yang menunjukkan bahwa kepadatan vektor di lingkungan sasaran masih tinggi dan memerlukan penguatan upaya pengendalian lingkungan, termasuk penerapan 3M Plus secara berkelanjutan. Sebanyak 87,5% peserta menyatakan bersedia melanjutkan pemantauan ovitrap secara mandiri setelah kegiatan berakhir. Program SIYAGA menunjukkan potensi dalam memperkuat surveilans vektor berbasis masyarakat dan mendukung deteksi dini keberadaan Aedes spp. Mengingat masih ditemukannya ketidaktepatan pemasangan ovitrap pada sebagian peserta serta tingginya nilai OI, program ini direkomendasikan untuk dilanjutkan melalui pendampingan rutin, integrasi dengan kegiatan pemantauan jentik berkala, dan penguatan peran kader kesehatan di masyarakat.
journal: Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pengembangan Masyarakat Indonesia

Hasil menunjukkan bahwa skor pengetahuan peserta (n=40) meningkat dari rata-rata 50,3 ± 12,4 pada pre-test menjadi 88,1 ± 8,6 pada post-test. Sebagian besar peserta mampu memasang ovitrap dengan benar dan 90,0% peserta mengikuti seluruh tahapan kegiatan yang meliputi edukasi, pelatihan pembuatan ovitrap, pemasangan ovitrap, dan minimal tiga dari empat kali pemantauan mingguan. Nilai Ovitrap Index meningkat dari 52,5% pada minggu pertama menjadi 62,5% pada minggu keempat, yang menunjukkan bahwa kepadatan vektor di lingkungan sasaran masih tinggi dan memerlukan penguatan upaya pengendalian lingkungan, termasuk penerapan 3M Plus secara berkelanjutan. Sebanyak 87,5% peserta menyatakan bersedia melanjutkan pemantauan ovitrap secara mandiri setelah kegiatan berakhir. Program SIYAGA menunjukkan potensi dalam memperkuat surveilans vektor berbasis masyarakat dan mendukung deteksi dini keberadaan Aedes spp. Mengingat masih ditemukannya ketidaktepatan pemasangan ovitrap pada sebagian peserta serta tingginya nilai OI, program ini direkomendasikan untuk dilanjutkan melalui pendampingan rutin, integrasi dengan kegiatan pemantauan jentik berkala, dan penguatan peran kader kesehatan di masyarakat.

title: Doenças tropicais negligenciadas: livros didáticos e divulgação científica no ensino médio
abstract: O estudo analisou como as Doenças Tropicais Negligenciadas (DTNs) são abordadas em livros de Ciências da Natureza do Ensino Médio em Floriano (PI) e desenvolveu ações socioeducativas de prevenção. Foram examinados seis livros da coleção Moderna Plus, utilizados em escolas públicas. Constatou-se abordagem superficial, com lacunas em transmissão, prevenção, tratamento e interdisciplinaridade. O livro L2 apresentou maior cobertura, enquanto L5 e L6 quase não mencionaram o tema. Essa ausência compromete a formação crítica dos estudantes e a compreensão de aspectos sociais e ambientais das DTNs. Para suprir a deficiência, o projeto realizou palestras com metodologias participativas e recursos visuais sobre doenças como ascaridíase, pediculose e dengue, ampliando o conhecimento e incentivando práticas preventivas. Também houve divulgação científica pelo Instagram (@parasitoses_ctf), com postagens educativas que obtiveram boa interação. Conclui-se que é urgente ampliar a presença das DTNs nos materiais didáticos e fortalecer práticas integradas de educação e saúde.

title: Estrategias de prevención comunitaria de enfermedades transmitidas por vectores en Paraguay: determinantes socioambientales y efectividad de intervenciones
abstract: Las enfermedades transmitidas por vectores, principalmente el dengue, chikungunya, zika y leishmaniasis visceral, constituyen un problema prioritario de salud pública en Paraguay. Su carácter endémico y la frecuencia creciente de brotes epidémicos exigen comprender los determinantes socioambientales de su transmisión y la efectividad de las estrategias preventivas comunitarias. El objetivo de este trabajo es sintetizar y evaluar la evidencia disponible sobre la situación epidemiológica y las intervenciones implementadas en el país. Se realizó una revisión narrativa descriptiva con búsqueda sistemática en bases de datos e instituciones oficiales, seleccionando estudios publicados entre 2020 y 2025. Los resultados muestran que la movilización vecinal y el enfoque de comunicación para el impacto conductual reducen los índices larvarios en el corto plazo; sin embargo, persiste una brecha entre conocimientos y prácticas sostenibles, así como fatiga comunitaria en periodos interepidémicos. Las deficiencias en saneamiento, suministro de agua y gestión de residuos limitan significativamente el impacto de las acciones. Se concluye que las estrategias comunitarias son necesarias, pero requieren políticas sanitarias permanentes e intersectoriales que articulen participación ciudadana con mejoras sostenidas en los servicios públicos básicos.
journal: LATAM Revista Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades

title: Development of an infection via sugar meal (IVSM) technique to infect mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) with arthropod-borne viruses
abstract: The global expansion of mosquito vectors is increasing human exposure to arboviruses, highlighting the need for rapid and practical approaches to assess vector competence. Standard artificial laboratory infection methods rely on infectious blood meals or intrathoracic inoculation, both of which can be resource-intensive and limit the capacity to conduct timely experiments, particularly in high-containment facilities. We developed an infection via sugar meal (IVSM) technique to determine whether mosquitoes can acquire and transmit arboviruses by ingesting virus-spiked sucrose. Using IVSM, we tested the vector competence of Aedes albopictus and Culex quinquefasciatus for West Nile virus (WNV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) following 1-hour or 24-hour exposures. Viral RNA copy numbers were quantified in the body, legs/wings, and saliva at 7 and 10 days post-infection. Both species supported WNV infection and dissemination, with the virus detected in saliva. Aedes albopictus exhibited high MAYV infection and dissemination rates, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus was largely refractory. ZIKV infection and dissemination were limited in both species and did not progress to saliva. High feeding success, low vector mortality, and reproducible outcomes across trials demonstrate that IVSM is an accessible and practical alternative to blood-based infection models and provides a framework for investigating vector competence under conditions that utilize natural feeding behavior.

title: Diagnostic capacity and safety implications of a clinical decision-support tool for febrile returning travelers: lessons learned from the FeverTravelApp evaluation
abstract: Ce travail évalue FeverTravelApp (FTAPP), un outil d’aide à la décision clinique destiné à soutenir les médecins non spécialistes lors de la prise en charge initiale de voyageurs et migrants présentant une fièvre au retour d’une région tropicale ou subtropicale. L’objectif était de comparer rétrospectivement les diagnostics, examens complémentaires et traitements antibiotiques proposés par FTAPP lors de l’évaluation initiale avec ceux retenus dans la cohorte prospective multicentrique européenne EFFORT, menée entre 2017 et 2019 à Barcelone, Anvers et Lausanne. Après application des critères d’exclusion, 738 patients ont été inclus dans les analyses. FTAPP a été appliqué aux données disponibles lors de la consultation initiale. Les diagnostics proposés, investigations recommandées et prescriptions antibiotiques ont ensuite été comparés aux données EFFORT, avec une attention particulière portée aux diagnostics graves ou nécessitant une prise en charge rapide. La concordance diagnostique globale était modérée et augmentait lorsque l’analyse était limitée aux diagnostics relevant du champ de FTAPP. Plusieurs discordances concernaient néanmoins des maladies potentiellement importantes, notamment certaines rickettsioses, la dengue, la fièvre typhoïde et le paludisme. Ces divergences peuvent notamment s’expliquer par le compromis entre sensibilité et spécificité des critères utilisés par l’algorithme, la prise en compte limitée de la sévérité des symptômes, la difficulté à intégrer l’évolution temporelle des maladies et les différences entre logique algorithmique et raisonnement clinique face à des présentations complexes ou atypiques. Des différences ont également été observées concernant les examens complémentaires et les prescriptions antibiotiques. Leur interprétation était toutefois limitée par la nature différente des stratégies comparées : EFFORT s’inscrivait dans un contexte de recherche visant à établir le diagnostic final de la manière la plus complète possible, tandis que FTAPP est destiné à soutenir la prise en charge clinique. Ces résultats montrent les limites d’une validation rétrospective comparant les propositions d’un outil au moment de la consultation initiale avec un diagnostic final établi plusieurs semaines plus tard. Une évaluation prospective paraît plus appropriée, en documentant les décisions cliniques avant et après utilisation de FTAPP et en évaluant non seulement la concordance diagnostique, mais également la sécurité, la pertinence des investigations et traitements ainsi que l’influence réelle de l’outil sur la prise de décision. Les outils d’aide à la décision clinique doivent ainsi être considérés comme des supports destinés à structurer et compléter le raisonnement médical plutôt que comme des substituts au jugement clinique.

Plusieurs discordances concernaient néanmoins des maladies potentiellement importantes, notamment certaines rickettsioses, la dengue, la fièvre typhoïde et le paludisme. Ces divergences peuvent notamment s’expliquer par le compromis entre sensibilité et spécificité des critères utilisés par l’algorithme, la prise en compte limitée de la sévérité des symptômes, la difficulté à intégrer l’évolution temporelle des maladies et les différences entre logique algorithmique et raisonnement clinique face à des présentations complexes ou atypiques. Des différences ont également été observées concernant les examens complémentaires et les prescriptions antibiotiques. Leur interprétation était toutefois limitée par la nature différente des stratégies comparées : EFFORT s’inscrivait dans un contexte de recherche visant à établir le diagnostic final de la manière la plus complète possible, tandis que FTAPP est destiné à soutenir la prise en charge clinique. Ces résultats montrent les limites d’une validation rétrospective comparant les propositions d’un outil au moment de la consultation initiale avec un diagnostic final établi plusieurs semaines plus tard. Une évaluation prospective paraît plus appropriée, en documentant les décisions cliniques avant et après utilisation de FTAPP et en évaluant non seulement la concordance diagnostique, mais également la sécurité, la pertinence des investigations et traitements ainsi que l’influence réelle de l’outil sur la prise de décision. Les outils d’aide à la décision clinique doivent ainsi être considérés comme des supports destinés à structurer et compléter le raisonnement médical plutôt que comme des substituts au jugement clinique.

title: V-SWITCH: A single-vector OFF-to-ON fluorescent reporter of live RNA virus infections
abstract: Fluorescent reporters of viral infection are powerful tools for studying viral pathogenesis and host-pathogen interactions. Here, we present V-SWITCH, a highly modular, single-vector, cell-based OFF-to-ON fluorescent reporter that enables robust detection of viral infection in living cells. V-SWITCH is based on a split mNeonGreen (mNG) system employing a release-and-capture mechanism. In the "OFF" state, the mNG3A(1-10) fragment is anchored to the endoplasmic reticulum via a Sec61 transmembrane domain, while the mNG(11) fragment, fused to BFP, is constitutively expressed in the nucleus. Upon infection, the viral protease cleaves a protease cleavage site (PCS) adjacent to the mNG3A(1-10) fragment, liberating it for translocation into the nucleus. There, it complements mNG(11) to reconstitute fluorescence. The constitutive BFP serves as both an expression control and a nuclear segmentation marker for image analysis. Each module in this dual-cassette design is flanked by unique restriction sites allowing rapid swapping of virus-specific PCS, split fluorophores, membrane anchors, and promoters. We demonstrate the versatility of the V-SWITCH reporter for several viruses (Dengue virus, Zika virus, West Nile virus and Human Coronavirus OC43) in several cell lines (A549, BJ-5 fibroblasts, HEK293T and HeLa). Reporter activation enables clear discrimination of infected and uninfected cells by flow cytometry and reveals time-dependent and heterogeneous infection dynamics by live-cell imaging at single-cell resolution. Importantly, we demonstrate the potential of V-SWITCH to support both rapid functional screening for host factor dependencies, as well as high-throughput compound screening to enable antiviral discovery and comparative evaluation of therapeutic strategies across multiple viruses and cell types.

media_mentions.content_title: Caregiver Misconceptions and Delayed Hospital Presentation Associated With Severe Dengue Among Hospitalised Children in Bangladesh
media_mentions.content: Abstract Background: Dengue remains a major cause of hospitalisation and severe illness among children in Bangladesh. Caregivers' recognition of warning signs, decisions to seek healthcare, and use of traditional remedies can significantly affect disease progression. This study assessed gaps in caregivers' knowledge, the use of traditional remedies, and factors associated with severe dengue and delayed hospital presentation among hospitalised children. Methodology: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 390 children with laboratory-confirmed dengue admitted to two tertiary care centres in Dhaka between June and December 2025. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics, healthcare-seeking pathways, traditional practices, and caregiver knowledge. The primary outcomes were severe dengue and delayed hospital presentation, defined as presentation >4 days after illness onset. Multivariable binary logistic regression models were fitted using 384 complete cases to identify independent predictors of severe disease and delayed presentation. Results: Severe dengue was identified in 98 children (25.1%), while 142 children (36.4%) presented after the fourth day of illness. Substantial knowledge gaps were evident, including poor recognition of warning signs in 352 (90.3%), lack of recognition of shock signs in 289 (74.1%), and limited critical-phase awareness in 379 (97.2%). Traditional or non-medical remedies were used in 261 cases (66.9%). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, delayed hospital presentation (>4 days) emerged as a strong independent risk factor for severe dengue (adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = 9.45, 95% confidence interval (CI): 5.12-17.44, P < 0.001), alongside travel-related delay (AOR = 4.68, 95% CI: 2.69-8.13, P < 0.001). Furthermore, the misconception that clinical recovery occurs after fever subsides (AOR = 3.71, 95% CI: 2.25-6.12, P < 0.001) and travel barriers (AOR = 4.52, 95% CI: 2.68-7.63, P < 0.001) were significant independent predictors of delayed hospital presentation. Conclusions: Widespread cognitive misconceptions and structural barriers were significantly associated with delayed hospital presentation and severe dengue among children in Dhaka. Paediatric dengue management and community health strategies must prioritise targeted parental education, focusing on recognising clinical warning signs, understanding critical disease progression around defervescence, and seeking prompt medical care. Introduction Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection with a wide clinical spectrum. It ranges from a self-limiting febrile illness to severe dengue, characterised by plasma leakage, shock, severe bleeding and organ impairment. Deterioration typically occurs around defervescence, when fever falls and marks the start of the critical phase. Warning signs at this stage require urgent medical assessment [1]. Children are particularly affected. A Global Burden of Disease 2021 analysis found that dengue incidence and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were consistently higher in children and adolescents than in the whole population between 1990 and 2021. Dengue-related DALYs in this age group rose by about 16% over that period, with the highest burden in middle- and low-middle-Socio-demographic Index (SDI) regions [2]. Bangladesh illustrates this changing burden. After sporadic transmission until 1999, dengue outbreaks have occurred with increasing frequency since 2000. The 2019 epidemic was the largest recorded at that time, and climate change, unplanned urbanisation, high population density, and a strained health system were proposed contributors, along with a need to train clinicians to manage severe dengue [3]. Hsan et al. reported that Bangladesh recorded its highest-ever number of dengue cases in 2023, with 321,179 cases and 1,705 deaths, of which approximately 10% occurred in children aged up to 10 years [4]. Data on children are more limited. A Bangladeshi paediatric study described clinical and haematological differences between dengue fever and dengue haemorrhagic fever. Its authors noted that paediatric clinical reports had been scarce and came mainly from Dhaka [5]. In our own study of 346 hospitalised children at Mugda Medical College Hospital in 2024, 15.3% had severe dengue. Raised haematocrit, pleural effusion, ascites, thrombocytopenia, hypoalbuminaemia and elevated transaminases were the strongest independent predictors, indicating that severe disease reflects plasma leakage and organ involvement [6]. That study examined only clinical, laboratory and radiological predictors, not caregiver or pre-hospital factors. Severity is influenced by viral, immunological and host factors. However, the timing and appropriateness of care before admission may be modifiable determinants. In a multicentre study of 1,313 hospitalised patients during Bangladesh’s 2023 epidemic, 19.3% had severe dengue. Low family income and lack of awareness contributed [7]. Delayed care-seeking is also a wider issue in childhood fever. In India, nearly one-third of caregivers sought treatment for children under five more than 24 hours after fever onset. Greater distance to a health facility was strongly associated with delay [8]. A mixed-methods study of parents of children with dengue in the Philippines found that financial constraints, previous dengue infection, transport, location and facility capacity contributed to delays. The study recommended public education about dengue symptoms and the importance of seeking care early [9]. However, the study was small, with only 24 respondents, and both dengue-specific studies were conducted outside Bangladesh. A national survey of 1,010 adults in Bangladesh found that most had heard of dengue and had moderate knowledge of its vectors and symptoms. However, their preventive practices were poor [10]. These findings do not indicate whether caregivers recognise warning signs or the critical phase of dengue. Nor do they show how caregivers’ beliefs affect decisions about seeking care for a sick child. Hospital studies conducted in Bangladesh during recent outbreaks have described clinical, laboratory, demographic and socioeconomic profiles [4-7]. They have not systematically examined caregivers’ beliefs or the care pathway before hospital admission. Evidence on delayed presentation comes from studies of non-dengue febrile illness [8] or from small-scale or qualitative studies conducted elsewhere [9]. To our knowledge, no study in Bangladesh has used adjusted analysis to quantify the links between specific caregiver misconceptions, initial healthcare-seeking behaviour, access-related barriers, delayed hospital presentation and severe dengue among hospitalised children. To address these critical gaps, this study had two primary objectives: first, to systematically assess caregivers’ baseline knowledge, awareness and traditional remedy practices; and second, to identify independent predictors and quantify their associations with the two primary outcomes of interest: delayed hospital presentation and progression to severe dengue among hospitalised children. Materials & Methods Study design and setting This hospital-based, cross-sectional observational study included children with laboratory-confirmed dengue who were admitted to two tertiary care hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh: Mugda Medical College Hospital and Insaf Barakah Hospital. The study was conducted from June to December 2025. Mugda Medical College Hospital is a government tertiary hospital that primarily serves lower- and middle-income urban and peri-urban populations. Insaf Barakah Hospital is a private hospital that serves a more socioeconomically diverse population. Both hospitals receive patients from Dhaka and surrounding districts. Participants were consecutively enrolled upon hospital admission. Severe dengue was diagnosed and classified daily in accordance with the World Health Organization (WHO) 2009 criteria, based on clinical signs, laboratory parameters and hospital tracking records. The date of symptom onset was established through standardised caregiver recall of the initial fever, and delayed presentation was prespecified as more than four days after symptom onset, reflecting the critical transition phase of dengue pathogenesis. Study population and sampling Children aged ≤18 years with laboratory-confirmed dengue were eligible. Dengue infection was confirmed by a positive NS1 antigen test and/or dengue-specific IgM according to hospital diagnostic protocols. We included primary caregivers who provided written informed consent and were available for interview during the hospital stay. Caregivers who declined participation or could not provide reliable information because of severe emotional distress, altered mental status or communication difficulties were excluded. Consecutive sampling was used to enrol eligible participants. The minimum sample size (N = 384) was calculated using the standard formula for a cross-sectional study, assuming an anticipated prevalence of 50%, a 95% confidence level and a 5% margin of error. The target sample size was increased to 390 participants to account for potentially incomplete data. Furthermore, severe dengue was diagnosed and classified daily in accordance with the WHO 2009 criteria. Data collection Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a structured, pre-tested questionnaire (Appendices A-B). The questionnaire was developed with reference to WHO dengue guidelines [1] and previous literature on dengue knowledge and healthcare-seeking behaviour [8,9]. It was pre-tested with 20 caregivers and showed good internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.82). The questionnaire covered child characteristics, caregivers’ sociodemographic factors, healthcare-seeking behaviour, barriers to accessing care, traditional and other non-medical practices, and caregivers’ knowledge and beliefs about dengue. Child-level clinical information was obtained from caregivers and, where available, hospital records. Questionnaires assessing caregiver knowledge were adapted from validated tools in prior regional studies, with internal reliability confirmed via pilot testing (α > 0.80). The questionnaire and its structural components were formally reviewed, validated, and approved by the Institutional Ethics Review Board prior to study commencement as part of the formal ethical clearance process. Caregiver warning-sign recognition was classified as 'good' if respondents correctly identified ≥3 WHO-defined warning signs and 'poor' if fewer than three were identified. Critical-phase awareness was defined as recognising the high-risk window occurring around defervescence (days 3-5). Variables and operational definitions The primary outcome was severe dengue, defined according to WHO 2009 criteria [1]. Children who did not have severe dengue were classified as having non-severe dengue, regardless of whether they had warning signs. The date of symptom onset was established through standardised caregiver recall of the initial fever. Delayed presentation was prespecified as >4 days after onset, reflecting the critical transition phase of dengue pathogenesis. Child-level variables included hospital, sex, age, comorbidity and day of illness at presentation. Age was categorised as <5, 5-10 and >10 years. Comorbidity included clinically significant conditions such as asthma, congenital heart disease, diabetes, neurological disorders and malnutrition; malnutrition was assessed according to WHO child growth standards [11]. Caregiver education was categorised as ≤primary or ≥secondary education, and residence as urban Dhaka, Dhaka slum or outside Dhaka. Monthly household income was categorised as <15,000, 15,000-25,000 or >25,000 BDT. These categories follow the classification used in the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES) 2022 [12]. Delayed presentation was defined as arrival at the study hospital more than 4 days after illness onset. Presentation by day 4 was classified as non-delayed. Referral to a tertiary hospital after day 4 did not, by itself, constitute delayed presentation if appropriate medical assessment had taken place earlier. Initial healthcare-seeking behaviour was classified as doctor or hospital, pharmacy, social media or the internet, or a traditional healer. Access- and travel-related delays included reported barriers involving distance, transport, financial constraints or difficulties with referral or access. Traditional and non-medical remedy use was analysed using the composite variable recorded in the dataset. Individual practices, including papaya leaf juice, papaya fruit extract, and the use of traditional healers and homoeopathy, were recorded separately. These practices were not mutually exclusive. Caregiver knowledge and beliefs covered recognition of dengue warning signs and signs of shock, awareness of the critical phase, and beliefs that a high fever indicates severe dengue and that recovery follows the subsidence of fever. Caregiver misconceptions were defined as incorrect or misleading beliefs about dengue progression or severity. Statistical analysis Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 29 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY). Categorical variables were reported as frequencies and percentages and compared using the chi-squared test or Fisher’s exact test, as appropriate. Continuous variables were reported as medians and interquartile ranges and compared using appropriate non-parametric tests. A two-sided P-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Two separate multivariable binary logistic regression models were performed. The first model examined factors associated with severe dengue, including age, comorbidity, delayed presentation, household income, use of traditional or non-medical remedies, recognition of warning signs and signs of shock, awareness of the critical phase, the misconception that high fever indicates severe illness, the belief that recovery occurs after fever subsides, and access- or travel-related delays. Day of illness was not included as a separate variable because delayed presentation was derived from it. The second model assessed factors associated with delayed hospital presentation, including hospital, residence, household income, caregiver education, use of traditional or non-medical remedies, initial healthcare-seeking behaviour, access- or travel-related delay, high-fever misconception, belief that recovery occurs after fever subsides, and warning-sign recognition. Candidate variables for multivariable modelling were selected based on biological plausibility, clinical relevance and bivariate screening (P < 0.20), with known confounders forced into the models to ensure simultaneous adjustment. A complete-case analysis was performed for the multivariable logistic regression models (N = 384), excluding six participants (1.5%) who declined to disclose their monthly household income. All six participants had delayed hospital presentation (>4 days); among them, three had severe dengue and three had non-severe dengue. These six participants were excluded from the multivariable regression analyses because of missing household income data. Ethical considerations The Institutional Ethics Review Board approved the study before it began. Written informed consent was obtained from all participating caregivers before data collection. Confidentiality was maintained throughout the study. Results This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 390 children who were admitted with dengue fever to two tertiary care centres in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Figure 1 shows the participant flow. The study assessed 460 eligible caregivers for inclusion. Seventy caregivers were excluded: 31 (44.3%) declined to participate, 22 (31.4%) faced communication barriers and 17 (24.3%) experienced emotional distress. The study enrolled the remaining 390 caregivers, who were included in the final analysis. Of the 390 participants, most presented with non-severe dengue (n = 292, 74.9%), while 98 (25.1%) developed severe dengue. The analysis examined sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, access and travel barriers, caregiver knowledge and misconceptions, and independent predictors of delayed hospital presentation and disease severity. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted using complete cases (N = 384). Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics by disease severity Table 1 outlines the distribution of sociodemographic and clinical characteristics by disease severity. The sample comprised 390 children: 292 (74.9%) had non-severe dengue and 98 (25.1%) had severe dengue. Children aged 5-10 years and those aged over 10 years accounted for substantial proportions in both groups. Overall, males slightly outnumbered females. Delayed hospital presentation, defined as seeking care more than four days after illness onset, was much more common among children with severe dengue. Overall, delayed presentation occurred in 142 patients (36.4%). It occurred in 74 of 98 patients (75.5%), compared with 68 of 292 patients (23.3%) with non-severe dengue. This difference showed that delayed clinical assessment was concentrated among children who developed severe complications. Caregiver characteristics and socioeconomic status Table 2 presents the socioeconomic backgrounds and caregiver characteristics of the study participants (N = 390), including six participants who did not disclose their monthly income. Most caregivers were mothers. Families fell into lower, middle and higher monthly household income brackets. However, a notable proportion of severe dengue cases came from lower-income households. Caregivers’ educational attainment varied. Lower educational attainment was positively correlated, in bivariate analysis, with delayed health-seeking behaviour and subsequent disease severity. Heal…
